argmax.description: The accepted serial two-stage argmax tree and original prompt/token assembly, independent of upstream numerical correctness. Inputs: input0=contiguous BF16 scores[151936], input1=contiguous int64 prompt[7], on the same CUDA device. The schedule selects logits row 6 without a cast. Returns selected int64 rank-zero tensor and tokens int64[1,8]. Retains all 96 chunks of 1600, 128 strided candidate lanes per chunk, the four-warp then two-stage chunk reduction and the 256-lane/eight-warp final reduction, invalid-index sentinels, and encoded chunk/local indices. Strictly greater finite comparisons preserve encounter/tree order on ties; NaNs win over non-NaNs and smaller encoded indices win among NaNs. The original empty-selection fallback and prompt copy are unchanged. Exact replay is extraction evidence, not proof of numerical equivalence or argmax stability for approximately related score vectors.

decoder.description: One parameterized complete Mirage attention/MLP decoder, preserving the accepted fused next-entry normalization boundary. Inputs input0..input6 are explicit BF16 weight slices: QKV[4096,1024], Q/K norm[256], attention output[1024,2048], post-attention RMSNorm[1024], gate/up[6144,1024], down[1024,3072], next-entry or final RMSNorm[1024]. input7=residual[8,1024], input8=already normalized entry[8,1024], input9=cosine[4096,128], input10=sine[4096,128], all BF16. input11 is the absolute rotary row offset, 0 in the accepted prefill, with 0<=input11<=4088. All tensors are contiguous on one CUDA device. Returns both new residual[8,1024] and normalized[8,1024]; neither may be omitted or substituted by a recorded tensor in reconstruction. The last occurrence supplies final-norm weights instead of next-layer entry-norm weights, without changing its implementation. Includes all eight grouped heads, seven valid tokens and the eighth padded row, Q/K normalization and rotary rounding, causal softmax, attention output, residual/RMSNorm, gate/up layout, rounded SiLU multiplication, down projection, and fused residual/next RMSNorm. The original mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16.row.col.f32.bf16.bf16.f32 instructions and accumulation order are unchanged; all ordinary numerical work remains serial. No persistent KV/recurrent state exists in this accepted prefill. Only residual and normalized are mutable carried state; immutable rotary tables and original prompt/weights stay live through explicit bindings. Scratch arrays are overwritten before reuse and are not live.

embedding.description: Seven-token Mirage embedding/positional setup plus entry RMSNorm. Inputs: input0=BF16 embedding weights[151936,1024], input1=int64 prompt[7] with token IDs in [0,151936), input2=BF16 entry norm weights[1024]. All tensors are contiguous on one CUDA device. Returns residual[8,1024], normalized[8,1024], cosine[4096,128], sine[4096,128], all BF16. The padded eighth residual row embeds token zero exactly as accepted. Compute the complete rotary tables for absolute positions 0..4095 with base 1000000, retaining every BF16 rounding and the serial RMSNorm tree. Entry normalization is grouped here because subsequent entry/final norms are already fused into the preceding decoder residual addition. Rotary tables remain immutable explicit inputs at all decoder cuts; weights and the prompt remain immutable original inputs. The full-program integer input2 is ignored by the accepted computation and retained by trace.cu.

projection.description: Final vocabulary projection and the original hidden-output copy. Inputs: input0=BF16 tied vocabulary weights[151936,1024], input1=BF16 final normalized state[8,1024], contiguous on one CUDA device. Final normalization has already occurred inside the last decoder's fused residual addition; do not normalize again. Returns the complete BF16 logits[8,153600] and hidden[7,1024]. All eight projected rows and padded vocabulary columns are retained; the original zero weight operands for columns >=151936 and exact MMA order are unchanged. Hidden copies the first seven normalized rows using the original serial finish loop. That independent copy is grouped with projection; the instrumented original still executes it in finish and snapshots its source at the projection cut. No argmax or approximate score substitution is performed here. The selected score row is an explicit schedule view.
